comment: Never-worse ratchet: the gate fails when the problem count is HIGHER than this, and never on errors alone. Lower it whenever you fix something; nothing forces it down. Re-measure with `node scripts/release-checks.mjs lint --write` in a clean git worktree, so gitignored sibling checkouts on disk are not counted. It fell from 41 to 15 on 2026-10-24 with the store-scorecard-caution work, and since then `eslint .` reads exactly the files the store scanner reads: eslint.config.mjs uses the scanner's own hardcoded ignore list (obsidianmd/eslint-plugin PR #158), so this number and the scorecard count the same source. The drop did not come from the ignore list, which lints the same 127 files as the old one: the settings tab redraws through one helper instead of the deprecated `display()`, removing every `no-deprecated`, and the eight `fetch` defaults import `obsidianFetch` explicitly, removing every `no-restricted-globals` (the rest is earlier fixes this number was never lowered for). Nothing is silenced: no eslint-disable exists for obsidianmd/*, no-deprecated or no-restricted-globals. The composition today, all warnings, 0 errors. Scorecard-relevant, 3 (the `settings-tab/prefer-setting-definitions` warning went when the tab moved to `getSettingDefinitions()` with the 1.13.4 floor, settings-redesign ticket 10): 3 `prefer-window-timers` in src/llm-transcript.ts (`withTimeout` and `realSleep`): this file runs on Node in every test suite and the nightly as well as in Obsidian, `window` does not exist on Node, and `window.setTimeout` there once lost every rate-limited page in the nightly (see the comments at those lines). Not on the scorecard, 5 `ui/sentence-case` false positives on names and examples the rule cannot know. Since 2026-11-03 (retro after Readwise ticket 21) its `brands` option is the rule's own `DEFAULT_BRANDS`, which the scanner uses, plus reMarkable, so it flags what the scanner flags: `e.g. qwen2.5vl:7b` (src/localhost-register.ts), `existing requests` (src/settings-tab.ts; `Tagged Sync Pro` went with the heading, now a definition's `heading:`, which the rule does not read), `Smith Prompting` (both Zotero pickers), and the domain in "From readwise.io/access_token." (src/settings-tab.ts, the token row's wording fixed in the Readwise spec §2), which the rule reads as the brand Readwise in lower case.
